newsitem.title: CHINA: ING confident on China insurance licence.
newsitem.headline: ING confident on China insurance licence.

text.p: A senior official of Dutch financial services group Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV (ING) on Tuesday said he was confident Beijing would grant ING a licence to sell insurance in China's potentially vast market.

ING Insurance already had representative offices and was applying to open branches in Beijing, Shanghai and southern Guangzhou city, ING Group executive board member Herman Huizinga told a news conference in Beijing.
"Are we confident of getting a licence? The answer is very short -- yes," Huizinga said but gave no details of when one was likely to be granted.
Beijing currently allows only two foreign insurance firms -- American International Assurance Co Ltd and Japan's Tokio Marine and Fire Insurance Co Ltd -- to issue policies.
Scores of other firms have set up representative offices and are waiting for official approval to start business.
China was caught between the need for effective regulation of its insurance market and the pressing need for long-term capital, Huizinga said.
"They need to find a way to speed up the process," he said, adding that China with its huge market had little to fear from fierce competition among a large number of foreign firms.

Chinese economists have called for caution in opening the market to foreign insurers, arguing the newcomers could overwhelm state-owned domestic insurers burdened by high taxes and investment restrictions.
